name: integer_beyond_u64
description: A ~30-digit integer far beyond u64::MAX must round-trip digit-for-digit through decode_protocol_event -> render(json/yaml), never parse->f64->reserialize.

name: high_precision_float
description: 0.1 written to 34 significant digits must not collapse to the float64 shortest round-trip "0.1".

name: negative_zero
description: -0.0 must keep its sign, not normalize to 0 or 0.0, when parsed and re-emitted. JSON keeps the literal exactly; YAML/plain render an integral-valued float as its integer, sign included.

name: negative_zero_integer
description: The bare integer spelling -0 must keep its sign too. Rust's serde_json fast-pathed bare integers through a native parse that dropped the sign until 1.0.154; a decoded -0 now retains its literal in every language.

name: u64_max_regression
description: u64::MAX already round-tripped correctly before this phase (i64/u64-range integers were never the bug); guard against a regression introduced by the fidelity work itself.

name: exponent_notation
description: Exponent form must survive verbatim, not be renormalized to a different (even numerically equal) exponent or decimal spelling. Deliberately written with an explicit '+' sign: a sign-less exponent ("6.022e23") is a documented Rust/serde_json limitation, see rust/src/tests.rs's signless_exponent_is_a_known_serde_json_limitation.

name: leading_zero_numeric_string
description: A numeric-looking JSON string (never valid as a bare JSON number literal) must stay a string end to end, never reinterpreted as a number.

name: bare_epoch_ns_number
description: AFDATA naming convention requires _epoch_ns as a decimal string (values exceed the 2^53-1 safe-integer range); writing it as a bare JSON number is a naming-convention violation that `afdata lint` rejects, but it is not a license for the decode/render layer to corrupt the digits. The nanosecond value below is deliberately beyond f64's exact-integer range.

name: currency_above_i64_falls_back_to_original_literal
description: Integer-required money formatting is bounded by signed i64 in every SDK. A larger decoded literal must keep its original key and exact digits instead of saturating or rounding through float64.

name: bytes_bounded_by_u64
description: Byte formatting accepts the full unsigned 64-bit range in every SDK, and a decoded integral float counts as an integer for byte and money suffixes alike. A larger integer literal keeps its original key and exact digits.

name: negative_zero_integer_suffixes_agree_with_native_zero
description: A numeric -0 is non-negative and formats as integer zero for bytes and Bitcoin amounts. Its JSON literal still retains the sign.

name: suffixes_without_arithmetic_keep_exact_decoded_digits
description: Appending a unit does not require float64 arithmetic. Percent, duration and small millisecond output retain exact digits, and decoded integral Bitcoin amounts format like native integral numbers.

name: zero_with_an_exponent_beyond_machine_range
description: Zero stays an exactly integral value even when its exponent does not fit a machine integer; canonical YAML/plain output must agree across SDKs without converting the exponent to a float.

name: fractional_epoch_literals_do_not_round_into_timestamps
description: Timestamp suffixes require exact integral values; a fractional literal that rounds to a whole float64 must retain its original key and digits.

name: integer_suffixes_do_not_round_decoded_float_literals
description: Integer-required suffixes must test the exact decoded value before formatting: float64 must not round a fractional byte count into an integer, change a currency unit, or move an out-of-range amount inside i64.

name: integral_float_literals_render_as_integers
description: YAML/plain render a float literal whose value is an integer below 1e21 as that integer, decided on the literal's text so digits beyond float64 survive (9007199254740993.0). Fractional values and magnitudes from 1e21 keep their literal. JSON keeps every literal exactly.

name: unsigned_exponents_render_with_an_explicit_sign
description: A decoded exponent written without a sign renders with `e+`, the spelling every native float formatter uses, so a decoded and a native number of the same value render alike. Go, Python and TypeScript JSON keep the literal exactly; serde_json re-spells the exponent while scanning, which expected_json_rust records.

name: decoded_literals_take_the_shared_notation
description: YAML/plain place a decoded fractional literal's digits by the same [1e-6, 1e21) positional range a native number uses, so a literal and a native float of one value render alike. The digits as written survive, trailing zeros included; JSON keeps every literal exactly.

name: containers_inside_plain_arrays_use_the_canonical_number_form
description: Plain writes an object or array nested inside an array as compact JSON with sorted keys. Its number leaves take the same canonical form a scalar takes, so a decoded 1e5 reads 100000 and 1.0 reads 1 in every SDK, not each runtime's JSON spelling.

name: negative_zero_keeps_its_sign_with_a_unit
description: A decoded integer -0 renders as -0 with or without a unit suffix, the same text the canonical number form gives it as a scalar.

name: unit_suffixes_keep_numbers_beyond_float64
description: Appending a unit does no arithmetic, so a decoded literal beyond float64's range still takes its unit. Only _ms, which converts to seconds from 1000, needs a finite value and otherwise keeps its raw key and digits.
expected_plain: a=1e+400s b=1e+400ns c=1e+400μs d=1e+400% e="1e+400 minutes" f="1e+400 hours" g="1e+400 days" h_ms=1e+400

name: bitcoin_and_epoch_ns_integers_have_no_i64_bound
description: _sats, _msats and _epoch_ns take an integer of any size, as a number or a decimal string: Bitcoin amounts keep their exact digits, and _epoch_ns formats whenever the instant lies in RFC 3339's year range 0001-9999. A float literal counts when its value is an integer below 1e21.
